alumni.name: Stan Green
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Inaugural Class, 1987). Football Captain. Boston Herald and Boston Post All Scholastic team his senior season. Went on to play college football at Columbia.

alumni.name: John "Iron Mike" Harrington
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Inaugural Class, 1987). Two-time football captain. Boston Herald, Boston Globe, WESX, and North Shore All Scholastic team his senior season. Also an excellent baseball player. Athletic career ended after his senior season due to an accident. One of the greatest athletes to come out of Saugus.

alumni.name: Art Statuto
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class, 1989). Helped lead the Sachems to the 1941 Class C state championship. Went on to play college football at Notre Dame, where he was a member of their 1946 and 1947 National Champion football teams. He was selected to the 1948 college football All-Star Team. After graduating, he played professional football for three seasons with the Buffalo Bills (AAFC) and Los Angeles Rams (NFL) at the center position.

alumni.name: Doug Waybright
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class, 1988). Won State Championship in 1941 during his sophomore season. Was Captain his senior season. A 1943 Essex County All-Star. Went on to play college football at Notre Dame (1945, 1947-1949). Member of the 1947 and 1949 National Championship teams at Notre Dame. After college he served in the military before he returned to Saugus, where he was very active in youth sports. He was so beloved by the town that when he died at the young age of 38, officials named a new elementary school in his honor.

alumni.name: Art Spinney
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Inaugural Class, 1987). Went on to play college football at Boston College where he was Captain his senior season (1949). A 1972 Inductee into the Boston College Athletic Hall of Fame.
Played in the NFL for the Baltimore Colts (1950, 1953-1960) where he won several accolades:
3x All Pro (1958 - 1960)
2x Pro Bowl (1959 - 1960)
2x NFL Champion (1958 - 1959)
Was the Offensive Line Coach for the Boston Patriots from 1962 - 1968.

alumni.name: George Laskey
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Inaugural Class, 1987). 2x Sgt. Arthur Defranzo Player of the Year Award winner (1946-1947), Thomas Atkins Memorial Award 1946, named Boston Globe, Boston Post, Lynn Item, and North Shore All Scholastic teams in 1947.

alumni.name: Dan Murphy
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame inductee (Class of 1994). Named a Boston Globe and Lynn Item All-Scholastic in 1949.

alumni.name: Salvatore 'Sardi' Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Inaugural Class, 1987). A three-year starter at running back, Sal “Sardi” Nicolo became one of Massachusetts’ most celebrated high school football players. In a memorable senior season, he led his division in touchdowns and points, earned numerous All-Scholastic selections and received honorable mention High School All-American recognition.

His signature Sachems moment came in the 1949 Exchange Bowl, when he caught a 50-yard, over-the-shoulder touchdown pass from his brother Richie to tie Weymouth as time expired. Jimmy Kane’s extra point secured Saugus’ 7–6 victory and the Exchange Bowl championship. Nicolo also excelled in baseball.

He went on to play football at Louisiana State University from 1952 through 1954. His 94-yard touchdown run against Rice on October 4, 1952, remains a memorable achievement in LSU football history.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Richard “Richie” Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (1988). A Lynn Item All-Scholastic in 1950, Richard “Richie” Nicolo was a dual-threat quarterback who could beat opponents with both his arm and his legs. He led the Sachems to consecutive Exchange Bowl championships in 1949 and 1950.

In the 1949 Exchange Bowl, his 50-yard touchdown pass to his brother Sardi as time expired tied Weymouth. Jimmy Kane’s extra point completed the dramatic 7–6 victory. The following year, Richie threw two touchdown passes and rushed for two more scores in a 30–12 win over Brockton, earning the game’s Most Valuable Player honors.

Nicolo continued his college football career at Boston College and Louisiana State University (LSU).
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Christie Serino
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Inaugural Class, 1987). Set the career passing yards record at Saugus.
Went on to have a successful hockey coaching career. Coached in the Hockey East 1991 - 2005 (Assistant Coach at UNH 1991-1998; Head Coach at Merrimack 1999 - 2005).
Spent his final years as head coach, building Malden Catholic hockey program into a powerhouse (2005 - 2011). He led Malden Catholic to the Super 8 Championship in his final season in 2011.

alumni.name: Doug Mackie
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Inaugural Class, 1987). 2x Boston Globe, Boston Herald, and Lynn Item All Scholastic (1974-1975). Named to Parade Magazine and Blue Chip Magazine High School All American Team in 1975. Went on to play college football at Ohio State for the legendary Woody Hayes. Injuries cost him some playing time during his college days. Went on to play professionally in the NFL for the New York Giants (1982), New Orleans Saints (1986), and Atlanta Falcons (1987) although he was mostly a practice player in the NFL. His greatest success as a professional was in the USFL where he played for the Tampa Bay Bandits (1983) and the New Jersey Generals (1984-1985). While playing for the New Jersey Generals he was selected as a 1984 College & Pro Football Newsweekly 2nd Team All-Pro along with running back Herschel Walker as he was part of the starting offensive line who helped Walker set the still standing, single-season, pro football rushing record of 2,411 yards.

alumni.name: Steve Gannon
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class, 1988). Went on to play college football at Holy Cross. He was a standout member of the defense for the Holy Cross football team during the late 1970s. Earned first team All-ECAC honors during his senior year, in addition to receiving the Davitt Award as the team’s top defensive lineman. As a senior led the team with 143 tackles, the most in recorded school history at the time. During his junior year in 1978, he helped lead the Crusaders to an overall record of 7-4, including victories over Air Force, Army and Boston College. A 2020 Inductee into the Holy Cross Athletic Hall of Fame. After college he had two NFL tryouts, one with the New York Giants and one with the Cincinnati Bengals both in 1980. After his playing days ended he got involved in coaching youth and high school football, being an assistant coach on John Nicolo's Sachems teams (2001-2004).

alumni.name: John Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Inaugural Class, 1987)
A two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic (1974, 1975) and 1975 Thom McCann North Shore Player of the Year and Boston Herald All-Scholastic, he captained Saugus to the Northeastern Conference Championship.
At Ithaca College, he starred in football and baseball: All-American running back on the 1979 Stagg Bowl (Division III National) champions; College World Series MVP on the 1980 Division III National Championship baseball team.
Three-time Ithaca College Athletic Hall of Fame inductee (1986 individual; 2014 football team; 2019 baseball team).
Later contributions: Rebuilt Saugus Pop Warner program; Saugus Sachems head football coach (2001–2004); interim Saugus High School Athletic Director (2003–2004).

alumni.name: Steve Peach
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class, 1991). A 3x Lynn Item All Scholastic (first player to ever make the team 3x). Greatest QB to ever come out of Saugus High. Was also an excellent baseball and basketball player. He was heavily recruited by Syracuse and Boston College, and he decided on going to Syracuse, where he started as a freshman. After that, he transferred to Boston College as a junior and was the backup to Doug Flutie and was also the punter.

alumni.name: Darren McCullough
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class of 1997).

Darren McCullough ranks among the best all-around players in Sachems history and is one of the few Saugus players to earn Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors twice.

As a junior in 1985, he recorded 123 tackles and four interceptions while playing linebacker and defensive back. On offense, he rushed for 442 yards and added 232 receiving yards, finishing with six total touchdowns.

As a senior in 1986, McCullough again led the team in tackles and rushed for 1,081 yards and 11 touchdowns. His standout performance came against Danvers, when he rushed for 225 yards and four touchdowns while also making 16 tackles. That effort earned him the Item/Coca-Cola Gold Helmet Award.

alumni.name: Marc Fauci
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class, 2000). A 2x Lynn Item All Scholastic. Boston Globe All Scholastic his senior season. Won the NEC Most Valuable Player Award in football during his senior year. A 2x co-captain as a junior and senior. Went on to play college football for Boston University. Led the Terriers football team during arguably its best season ever in 1993 when BU went 12-1 and finished the regular season with a perfect 11-0 mark, the first unbeaten and untied record in program history. A second-team All-America selection by The Sports Network and National Weekly Football Gazette and a third-team All-America selection by the Associated Press, Fauci played linebacker and ranks in the top five for career primary, assisted and total tackles. Was a 2010 Inductee into the Boston University Athletic Hall of Fame.

alumni.name: Dan Schena
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class of 2001). A Lynn Item All-Scholastic in 1990, Dan Schena was a tri-captain and the heart and soul of the Sachems’ 8–2 team, whose season remains a highlight in the program’s history.

Regarded as one of the finest linemen to wear a Sachems jersey, Schena recorded more than 100 tackles during his senior season. He continued his football career at Northeastern University.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Mike Mabee
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame inductee (Class of 2006) and Lynn Item All-Scholastic. A multi-sport star at Saugus High School. As co-captain and standout quarterback of the 1995 Sachems, Mabee helped end a school-record 34-game losing streak and led Saugus to a 6–5 finish—the program’s first winning season since 1990.

alumni.name: LJ McKanas
alumni.bio: Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class, 2007). Captain his senior season. Played a big role in turning Saugus into a competitive program in the mid-90s. During his senior season he set records for most rushing yards and most touchdowns. He was selected Boston Globe, Boston Herald, and Lynn Item All-Scholastic. He then went on to play college football at Northeastern University. After he redshirted his freshman season, he went on to become a four-year starter. During his redshirt freshman season he broke the NU rookie rushing record with 832 yards, averaging 92.4 yards per game. His Sophomore and Junior seasons were derailed due to injuries. During his senior season he set school records for most carries, 342, rushing yards, 1756, and rushing touchdowns, 14. For his senior season, he was named team MVP, All-New England, All-Conference and first-team Hanson All-America. He was also the winner of the Harry Agganis Award as the Outstanding Senior Football Player in New England. After college he appeared on the TV Show "Survivor" in 2014 where he finished in 9th place.

alumni.name: Anthony “Beave” Barbanti
alumni.bio:
A two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Anthony “Beave” Barbanti was a three-year starter on both the offensive and defensive lines and a cornerstone of the Sachems during his junior and senior seasons.

His senior season in 2003 was his finest: he recorded 75 tackles, including 11 tackles for loss, and three sacks. He was equally dominant on the offensive line, helping clear the way for Mike Nicolo’s record-setting rushing performances. Barbanti’s strength, consistency and two-way play made him a key part of Saugus’ success.
alumni.source: Profile supplied by Sal Nicolo; senior statistics corroborated by the 2003 Item All-Star clipping.

alumni.name: Mike Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Hall of Fame Inductee (Class, 2026). A four-year starter and team captain his senior year, he set a then–single-game rushing record with 306 yards against Salem as a junior. He earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors that same season. Though injuries limited his senior year, his athletic success extended beyond football—he was an All-Scholastic selection in Winter Track as a sophomore and in Baseball as a junior.
He continued his football career at Curry College, where he was part of four consecutive New England Football Conference championship teams. He also contributed to Curry’s first-ever NCAA Division III playoff victory—fittingly, against his father John’s alma mater, Ithaca College.

alumni.name: Brett Reid
alumni.bio:
A three-year starting quarterback and two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Brett Reid helped lead a resurgence in Sachems football. As a junior in 2007, he teamed with Tyler Trainer, Paul Sullivan and Mike Dean to guide Saugus to a 7–3 record—its first winning season since 1997 and its most wins since 1996.

Operating in a run-heavy offense, Reid rushed for 797 yards and 13 touchdowns that season. He and Dean helped Saugus repeat its 7–3 finish in 2008, with Reid contributing 800 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Justin Winn
alumni.bio:
Justin Winn earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors in both his junior and senior seasons. In 2013, he rushed for 1,108 yards and 19 touchdowns, providing a standout individual performance during a difficult 3–9–1 season for the Sachems.

In 2014, Winn and running back Dan Cicciola helped lead Saugus to a 6–5 record. Winn rushed for 1,255 yards and set a school record with 22 rushing touchdowns.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Brandon Faiella
alumni.bio: A two-time captain and two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Faiella was named the Lynn Item Defensive Player of the Year as a senior. He continued his football career as a linebacker for the Saint Anselm College Hawks. As of fall 2026, he is in his junior season.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Carlo Abate
alumni.bio:
A three-year starter at linebacker and a two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Carlo Abate was a cornerstone of the Sachems’ defense. As a junior in 1994, he recorded more than 120 tackles, including 22 against Lynn English in a performance that earned him Gold Helmet player of the game honors.

Despite shoulder and knee injuries, Abate led the Saugus defense as a senior in 1995 with 115 tackles, four interceptions and four fumble recoveries. He played a key role in ending the Sachems’ 34-game losing streak and helping the team achieve its first winning season in five years.

stats.sourceNote: 1985 Item All-Star profile: 442 rushing yards, 232 receiving yards and six total touchdowns; rushing-only touchdown total not specified.
